basic_details.job_title: Indian Coast Guard Recruitment 2026 – Apply Offline for Engine Driver, MTS and More Posts
basic_details.short_information: Indian Coast Guard Regional Headquarters (East), Chennai, under the Government of India, Ministry of Defence, invites applications by Ordinary Post for five Group 'C' posts: Store Keeper Grade-II, Engine Driver, Lascar, Civilian Motor Transport Driver (Ordinary Grade) and MTS (MT Cleaner). Applications go to The Commander, Coast Guard Region (East), Near Napier Bridge, Fort St George (PO), Chennai - 600 009, and the last date of receipt of applications is 21 December 2026.

qualification.details: Age is counted as on the last date of receipt of applications, 21 December 2026. The category-wise vacancy tables are part of the notice, so check the official notification for the break-up of vacancies by category. | Educational qualification: 12th Pass from recognised Board or University. Essential experience: one year's experience in handling stores from any recognised firm or Central or State Govt. organisation or Public Sector undertaking. Age: 18 to 25 years (30 yrs for SC Category and 40 yrs for PwBD of SC category). Relaxable for Central Government Servants of SC category up to 45 years of age who have rendered at least 03 years continuous service under Government. | Educational qualification: Matriculation pass from a recognised Board or equivalent. Certificate of competency as Engine Driver from a recognised Government Institute or equivalent. Desirable: two years service as Sarang on a vessel of over four hundred Boat Horse Power. Age: 18 to 30 years, relaxable by 05 years for SC candidates. Relaxable for Central Government Servants of SC category up to 45 years of age who have rendered at least 03 years continuous service under the Government. | Educational qualification: Matriculation pass or its equivalent from recognised boards. Essential experience: three years experience in service on Boat. Age: 18 to 30 years for EWS Category. Relaxable for Central Government Servants of EWS category up to 40 years of age who have rendered at least 03 years continuous service under the Government. | Educational qualification: 10th pass from recognised Board, and a valid Driving License for both Heavy and Light Motor Vehicles. Essential experience: 02 years experience of driving. Knowledge of motor mechanism (should be able to remove minor defects in vehicles). Age: 18 to 27 years for UR Category. Relaxable for Central Government Servants of UR category up to 40 years of age and who have rendered at least 03 years continuous service under the Government. | Educational qualification: Matriculation pass from a recognized Board or equivalent. Essential experience: two years experience in mechanical workshop. Age: 18 to 27 years (32 years for SC Category and 42 years for PWBD of SC candidates). Relaxable for Central Government Servants of SC category up to 45 years of age who have rendered at least 03 years continuous service under the Government. | For the discipline-specific eligibility of each post, refer to the official notification.

selection_process: Part Subject Questions Marks Duration
I General Knowledge 20 20 01 Hour
II Mathematics 20 20 01 Hour
III General English 20 20 01 Hour
IV Relevant trade test for technical posts (SK-II, Engine Driver, Lascar, CMTD(OG)); Mental Ability Test for MTS (MT Cleaner) 20 20 01 Hour
Selection runs through scrutiny of applications
document verification
a written examination
a trade test where applicable
and a merit list.

All applications are scrutinised against the eligibility criteria and required documents. Admit cards or call letters are then issued to shortlisted candidates for document verification and the written examination. Shortlisted candidates bring their original documents
including the original admit card or call letter
and two sets of self-attested Xerox copies
as directed in the admit card.

Thumb impression and photograph are captured and verified at document verification or before entering the examination hall. Candidates whose biometric does not match at any stage are not allowed for the written examination
and refusal to take part may lead to cancellation of candidature. ICG reserves the right to capture or verify biometric data at other stages
and the Headquarters reserves the right to exempt biometric verification at any stage.
The written examination is pen-paper based and lasts one hour. The bilingual question paper has 80 objective type questions with one mark for each correct answer
and there is no negative marking. The syllabus follows the educational qualification and the relevant trade.
The qualifying mark in the written exam is 50%

and 45% for SC and ST candidates. No relaxation in qualifying marks is admissible to OBC and EWS candidates. Candidates who qualify the written test are shortlisted for the trade test (where applicable). The merit list is prepared strictly on merit position as per marks obtained in the written examination and is published on the Indian Coast Guard website with necessary instructions.
important_instructions: Check eligibility before applying. Wrong or false information leads to disqualification, and ICG is not responsible for the consequences. Candidature is liable to be rejected at any stage, or after recruitment or joining, if information is found false or not in conformity with the eligibility criteria. Applications are summarily rejected if incomplete, over aged on the last day of receipt, overwritten or corrected, without photographs affixed or self-attested, without self-attested photocopies of documents, or not superscribed on the envelope. SC/ST candidates are entitled to 2nd class rail / bus fare by shortest route as per Govt. rules, reimbursed at the written examination venue on submission of tickets. This is not admissible to SC/ST candidates already in Central/State Govt. service. Appearing or qualifying in the written examination does not give a right to claim appointment unless the candidate meets the eligibility criteria. Candidates selected for a Group 'C' post are liable for posting initially at any unit / establishment under Coast Guard Region (East), with All India transfer liability. Updates on this recruitment will appear on the ICG website, indiancoastguard.gov.in.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: The duly filled application with all the requisite documents must be sent by Ordinary Post only to the address below. Address: The Commander, Coast Guard Region (East), Near Napier Bridge, Fort St George (PO), Chennai - 600 009 Postal mode: Ordinary Post only Form: the prescribed format at Annexure-I, filled in either English or Hindi, with a self-attested colour photograph affixed and a left-hand thumb impression and signature as the form asks Envelope: it must be superscribed in BOLD letters "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF" followed by the post (Store Keeper Grade-II, Engine Driver, Lascar, CMTD(OG) or MTS(MT Cleaner)) and the category applied for (UR/EWS/OBC (Non Creamy Layer)/SC/ST). The notice gives a sample envelope at Annexure-V, and applications without these notations are summarily rejected. Government employees: candidates working in Govt. departments must forward their application through proper channel only, before the due date of receipt and along with an NOC issued by the concerned authority.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Attach Xerox copies of the documents below, each self-attested with name and date. No original certificates are to be forwarded along with the application form. Valid Photo ID proof (Aadhar/ PAN/ Voter ID/ Passport). Matriculation or equivalent mark sheet and certificate. 12th/UG/PG/Diploma mark sheet and certificate as per the essential eligibility. Latest Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC) for reserved category candidates. Experience certificate from the Govt. recognised firm with GST number. NOC from the employer, for those presently serving in any Govt. organisation. Two latest passport size colour photographs without sunglasses/ cap. The date of issue of all these documents must be on or before the closing date of application, 21 December 2026. Candidates in reserved categories must produce the category certificate in the prescribed format for appointment to a post under the Government of India; the formats are given at Annexures-II, III and IV (OBC, SC/ST and EWS income and asset certificate).

Shortlisted candidates bring their original documents, including the original admit card or call letter, and two sets of self-attested Xerox copies, as directed in the admit card. Thumb impression and photograph are captured and verified at document verification or before entering the examination hall. Candidates whose biometric does not match at any stage are not allowed for the written examination, and refusal to take part may lead to cancellation of candidature. ICG reserves the right to capture or verify biometric data at other stages, and the Headquarters reserves the right to exempt biometric verification at any stage. The written examination is pen-paper based and lasts one hour. The bilingual question paper has 80 objective type questions with one mark for each correct answer, and there is no negative marking. The syllabus follows the educational qualification and the relevant trade. The qualifying mark in the written exam is 50%, and 45% for SC and ST candidates. No relaxation in qualifying marks is admissible to OBC and EWS candidates. Candidates who qualify the written test are shortlisted for the trade test (where applicable). The merit list is prepared strictly on merit position as per marks obtained in the written examination and is published on the Indian Coast Guard website with necessary instructions.

faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for ICG Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date of receipt of applications is 21 December 2026. Applications must be sent by Ordinary Post only to The Commander, Coast Guard Region (East), Near Napier Bridge, Fort St George (PO), Chennai - 600 009.

faq.question: Q2. Which posts are covered by this ICG recruitment?
faq.answer: The posts are Store Keeper Grade-II, Engine Driver, Lascar, Civilian Motor Transport Driver (Ordinary Grade) and MTS (MT Cleaner), all General Central Service, Group 'C', Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for Store Keeper Grade-II?
faq.answer: 12th Pass from a recognised Board or University, plus one year's experience in handling stores from a recognised firm or a Central or State Govt. organisation or Public Sector undertaking.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification for Engine Driver?
faq.answer: Matriculation pass from a recognised Board or equivalent, and a certificate of competency as Engine Driver from a recognised Government Institute or equivalent. Two years service as Sarang on a vessel of over four hundred Boat Horse Power is desirable.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for ICG Lascar and Engine Driver?
faq.answer: Both have an age limit of 18 to 30 years, counted as on 21 December 2026. The Engine Driver limit is relaxable by 05 years for SC candidates, and the Lascar limit is printed for the EWS Category.

faq.question: Q6. What is the pay level for these posts?
faq.answer: Store Keeper Grade-II and Civilian Motor Transport Driver are in Pay Level-02, Engine Driver is in Pay Level-04, and Lascar and MTS (MT Cleaner) are in Pay Level-01 in the pay matrix.

faq.question: Q7. How are candidates selected?
faq.answer: Applications are scrutinised, and shortlisted candidates undergo document verification and a one-hour written examination of 80 objective questions. A trade test follows for qualifiers where applicable, and the merit list is based on written exam marks.

faq.question: Q8. Is there negative marking in the ICG written exam?
faq.answer: No. Each correct answer carries one mark and there is no negative marking. The qualifying mark is 50%, and 45% for SC and ST candidates.

faq.question: Q9. What must be written on the envelope?
faq.answer: Write "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF" with the post name, and the category applied for (UR/EWS/OBC (Non Creamy Layer)/SC/ST), in BOLD letters. Applications without these notations are summarily rejected.

faq.question: Q10. Should original certificates be sent with the application?
faq.answer: No. Send only self-attested Xerox copies with name and date; no original certificates are to be forwarded. Originals are brought at document verification by shortlisted candidates.
